name: Ignaz Forstmeier
current_role: Co-founder and former CMO, Personio; now with 3VC (Vienna software VC) and an angel investor
profile: One of four TU Munich/CDTM alumni who founded Munich HR-software company Personio in 2015 (with Hanno Renner, Roman Schumacher and Arseniy Vershinin); he served as CMO as it grew to an $8B valuation. Having left Personio's operations, he is based in Vienna, works with Series A fund 3VC and has angel-invested in 25+ startups.
interesting_fact: Personio grew out of the Center for Digital Technology and Management (CDTM) programme in Munich, which all four founders attended; Forstmeier was there 2013-2015.
deep_cut_fact: In Personio's early days, while hunting for their EUR 2.1M seed round, the founders went unpaid for a while; Forstmeier said fundraising is usually a full-time job for at least one founder. In 2016 customers grew from ~20 to 100+ purely through referrals, with no marketing budget.
notes: No longer operational at Personio; LinkedIn shows current affiliation with 3VC, Vienna. Low public profile.

name: Per Pettersen
current_role: Co-Founder, Chief Strategy Officer and Board Director, impact.com
profile: Serial ad-tech entrepreneur who co-founded Commission Junction (an early affiliate network, sold to ValueClick), then Leadpoint and Savings.com. In 2008 he co-founded Santa Barbara-based Impact Radius (now impact.com), a partnership-automation platform later valued at ~$2B. He was CEO until 2017, when he became executive chairman and CSO; impact.com now lists him as CSO.
interesting_fact: Impact Radius was founded by a group of Commission Junction alumni: Pettersen, Wade Crang, Todd Crawford, Lisa Riolo and Roger Kjensrud (now impact.com's CTO). In effect, the team that built one of the first affiliate networks rebuilt the category a decade later.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training, he holds a BS in electrical engineering and an MS in computer engineering from UC Santa Barbara. impact.com's own bio says he 'was building partnership businesses before the industry had a name for what he was doing.'
notes: Santa Barbara-based. No personal channels or published press email found; the impact.com contact page or press-releases section is the route in. The UCSB degrees appear in aggregated bios (e.g. a 2026 impact.com release, per search snippets); the full bio text could not be fetched directly.

name: Adam Hotchkiss
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, Plume (Palo Alto); interim CEO until April 2025
profile: Co-founded Plume at the end of 2014 with Fahri Diner, Aman Singla and Sri Nathan. Plume is a cloud-managed 'adaptive WiFi' and smart-home services platform sold through ISPs such as Comcast, Charter and Vodafone, reaching 65M+ locations, and was valued at ~$3B. He was interim CEO, then became CPO when ex-Comcast exec Daniel Herscovici was hired as CEO in April 2025.
interesting_fact: Plume's founding idea was to deconstruct the home router: move its 'brains' into the cloud and scatter small low-power pods around the home, an approach Plume calls 'Adaptive WiFi'.
deep_cut_fact: Before he became CPO, Plume's own technical whitepaper on its Adapt WiFi system listed him as 'Co-Founder, VP Product'. He has been the product mind behind the pods since day one.

public_contacts.value: ted_miller@tedmillergroup.com (Ted Miller Group, listed as Plume media contact)

notes: Low personal profile; best route is Plume corporate comms. Plume has done media interviews with him (e.g. plume.com interview on consumer engagement). The deep-cut fact is from search-result snippets of the whitepaper; the PDF itself was not opened.

name: Priyanka Gill
current_role: Founder & CEO, COLUXE (lab-grown diamond jewellery brand, launched 2025); co-founder, Good Glamm Group (MyGlamm)
profile: A former London-based journalist, Gill turned her blog eStylista into POPxo, a digital community for Indian women, after moving back to India in 2014. POPxo/Plixxo merged with MyGlamm in 2020 and became part of the Good Glamm Group in 2021, where she ran the media and content arm. She was later a venture partner at Kalaari Capital, then left in early 2025 to found COLUXE.
interesting_fact: COLUXE pitches AI-powered personalisation, virtual try-ons and modular jewellery, and has backers including Ajai Chowdhry (HCL co-founder) and Startup Sherpas.
deep_cut_fact: Born in a village in Punjab and an English Literature graduate of Lady Shri Ram College, she wrote for The Guardian, The Independent and Vogue India in London. She co-chaired the Pratham Gala (2009-10), which raised over GBP 3M. Her early collection of modern Indian art later sold at Christie's first auction in India.
notes: Media-friendly and active on social media. Her current focus is COLUXE (consumer/luxury), not the Good Glamm Group, so lead with COLUXE or her founder journey rather than Good Glamm's recent difficulties.

name: Tal Riesenfeld
current_role: Co-founder, Sunbit (Los Angeles-based point-of-sale financing); listed as Chief Revenue Officer/Head of Sales
profile: Israeli-born co-founder of Sunbit, a buy-now-pay-later platform for in-person purchases such as auto repair, dental and optical care, founded in 2016 with Arad Levertov, Ornit Dweck-Maizel and Prof. Tamir Hazan and valued at ~$1B+. He leads Sunbit's revenue/sales effort. Before Sunbit he co-founded video-ad company Eyeview (2008) and worked at HP and Google.
interesting_fact: Sunbit CEO Arad Levertov recruited Riesenfeld because they had known each other since childhood. Each of them put in $100,000 of his own money to start the company.
deep_cut_fact: Before Sunbit, he co-founded the video-advertising startup Eyeview in 2008, where he was VP of Sales, so Sunbit is his second venture-backed company.
notes: Low public profile; CEO Arad Levertov is Sunbit's public face. Riesenfeld's background (HBS MBA, HP, Google, Eyeview) comes from aggregator profiles such as TheOrg and Crunchbase. Route via Sunbit media@sunbit.com.

name: Pedro Bizarro
current_role: Co-Founder and Chief Science Officer, Feedzai (heads Feedzai Research)
profile: Portuguese computer scientist who co-founded Feedzai in Coimbra in 2011 with Nuno Sebastiao and Paulo Marques. Feedzai builds real-time machine-learning tools to detect payment fraud and financial crime for banks, retailers and e-commerce. It became a unicorn in 2021 and was valued above $2B in an October 2025 round. As Chief Science Officer he runs Feedzai Research (AI, data visualisation, systems).
interesting_fact: Feedzai was selected by the European Central Bank, together with Capgemini Germany, to provide the fraud and risk-management solution for the Digital Euro.
deep_cut_fact: Outside the lab he is an avid runner and an Ironman triathlete, per his Feedzai author bio.
notes: Technical founder who blogs on Feedzai's site and is a good fit for AI/data-infrastructure topics. No published press email found on feedzai.com; use the contact page or newsroom. Web-search quota ran out mid-lane, so research was limited to direct page fetches.

name: Ishay Green
current_role: Co-founder, OpenWeb (formerly Spot.IM); current operating role unclear (LinkedIn shows MGK Labs, Tel Aviv)
profile: Israeli software architect who co-founded Spot.IM with Nadav Shoval. Spot.IM was renamed OpenWeb in 2020 and builds hosted comment sections, community tools and ad products for publishers. OpenWeb passed a $1B valuation in its 2021 Series E and was valued at $1.5B+ in its 2022 Series F. Green keeps a low profile; his LinkedIn now describes him as an entrepreneur, investor and systems architect.
interesting_fact: OpenWeb's 2021 $150M round included The New York Times Company and NYU professor Scott Galloway among its investors, an unusual cap table for an ad-tech company.
notes: The LinkedIn profile (Tel Aviv; 'entrepreneur, investor, software & system architect'; MGK Labs; open-source HumanitarianGenome.org project) very likely belongs to him, but the fetched view did not show OpenWeb, so confirm before using it. Avoid OpenWeb's 2024 CEO dispute involving co-founder Nadav Shoval. No OpenWeb press email found.
